tagline: From a renamed spa town up to the emptied silver camps.
intro: The trail starts in Truth or Consequences, a desert town built over hot springs, and goes two ways from there. One arm runs out past Elephant Butte Dam and north through Cuchillo and Winston to the Beaverhead Ranger Station in the Gila National Forest. The other goes south by Caballo Lake, then west to Hillsboro and Kingston in the Black Range.

Gold and silver built the towns on both arms, and many of them have since emptied. Hillsboro was a gold camp in 1877 and the county seat until the 1930s, when the honor went to the town with the springs.

moments.title: Truth or Consequences
moments.text: In March 1950 the town of Hot Springs voted 1,294 to 295 to take the name of a radio quiz show. The host came back the first weekend of every May for 50 years.

moments.title: Elephant Butte Dam
moments.text: The dam takes its name from a volcanic plug said to look like an elephant lying on its side. The lake made an island of it, except at low water.

moments.title: Kingston
moments.text: Out the south arm, silver turned up in 1882, the camp soon had 1,800 people, and Lillian Russell once performed there. The 2020 census counted 50.
